what: The ordinary assistant's answers pharmadelta serves on the side-by-side page, one per question, each produced by a run of the frozen baseline (src/baseline/, a keyword matcher with no model, frozen at tag m00, SPEC/00 P5) made by this repository's CI, with the record of that run (milestones/M04/README.md). `answer` is what the run wrote for the question, verbatim; `row` and `clause` are copies of data/table.json and data/clauses.json at `data_commit` when the table holds the answer's row and the clauses hold its clause, else null. A number in this file is the row's or the clause's own data, or the run record's, never a measured result.
baseline: src/baseline/ of this repository: answer.py, keyword matching over the question, the table and the clauses; run.py, the runner. No model, no network, no randomness. Frozen at tag m00 and never improved (SPEC/00 P5). It is the control the agent is compared with. It is a keyword matcher, not an assistant, and the page says so (milestones/M00/rulings/pr2.md 1).
company: Ardentia Generics is fictional; its portfolio and every 'our label' statement are invented (SPEC/00 §2, §9)

lift.written_from: observations.json and result.json in that artifact; `uv run python -m src.m04.lift write --from <dir>` rebuilds this file and pages/side-by-side.html from them

answers.question: A competitor's metformin tablet label now lists an additional risk factor for lactic acidosis that the reference listed drug's label does not. May we add it to our metformin hydrochloride tablet label by CBE-0 under 21 CFR 314.70(c)(6)(iii)(A), and what do we owe?

clause.lead_in: (iii) Changes in the labeling to reflect newly acquired information, except for changes to the information required in § 201.57(a) of this chapter (which must be made under paragraph (b)(2)(v)(C) of this section), to accomplish any of the following:
clause.note: Changes being effected (CBE-0). The subject is 'the applicant' (314.3), which includes an ANDA applicant; 314.97(a) sends the ANDA holder here. Limited by the lead-in to newly acquired information.

answers.question:
Our distributor sent the note below about our metformin hydrochloride tablets. Does anything in it change what we owe on the label?

---
From: Regional distribution, Ardentia Generics (fictional)
Subject: Metformin HCl 500 mg, lot 24K117, carton shortfall

Three pharmacies in the southeast reported cartons of 30 arriving with 28 blisters. We have pulled the remaining stock of lot 24K117 from the Memphis warehouse and are counting it. The pharmacist at the second site also mentioned that one of her patients on our 500 mg tablets was admitted to hospital last week with hemolytic anemia and the attending physician has written it up as drug-related; she asked whether we wanted the details. Replacement cartons for all three sites ship Thursday. Please confirm whether we should hold the lot for the full count or release the verified cartons.

row.section_terms: lactic acidosis; renal impairment; concomitant carbonic anhydrase inhibitors; age 65 years or greater; radiological studies with contrast; surgery and other procedures; hypoxic states; excessive alcohol intake; hepatic impairment

clause.text: (iv) Comparison of approved and proposed labeling. A side-by-side comparison of the applicant's proposed labeling including, if applicable, any Medication Guide required under part 208 of this chapter with the approved labeling for the reference listed drug with all differences annotated and explained. Labeling (including the container label, package insert, and, if applicable, Medication Guide) proposed for the drug product must be the same as the labeling approved for the reference listed drug, except for changes required because of differences approved under a petition filed under § 314.93 or because the drug product and the reference listed drug are produced or distributed by different manufacturers. Such differences between the applicant's proposed labeling and labeling approved for the reference listed drug may include differences in expiration date, formulation, bioavailability, or pharmacokinetics, labeling revisions made to comply with current FDA labeling guidelines or other guidance, or omission of an indication or other aspect of labeling protected by patent or accorded exclusivity under section 505(j)(5)(F) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act.
clause.note: Sameness with the reference listed drug at submission, with the listed exceptions.
